In this assignment, you'll be picking up where you left off with the M&Ms activity. You'll load the data and perform some basic statistical analysis. Follow the steps below to complete the assignment.

### Task 1: Load the tidyverse
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

### Task 2: Load the M&Ms dataset from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dwillis/jour405/refs/heads/main/data/mandms.csv

```{r}
mandms <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dwillis/jour405/refs/heads/main/data/mandms.csv")
```

### Task 3: Sample 5 rows of data from the dataset

```{r}
set.seed(1234)

sample_5 <- sample_n(mandms, 5)

sample_5
```


### Task 4: Calculate the mean age and standard deviation of the sample, using either the red or black number of M&Ms

```{r}
mean(sample_5$red)

sd(sample_5$red)
```

### Task 5: Calculate the mean age and standard deviation of the population, using the same measure as in Task 4

```{r}
mean(mandms$red)

sd(mandms$red)
```

### Task 6: Compare the sample and population statistics

Compare the two sets of means and standard deviations. Are they similar?

The sample mean was 73.8, while the population mean was 72.98. These numbers are very close to each other. The sample standard deviation was 14.92314, compared to the population standard deviation of 16.45808. These results are also fairly similar. This shows that my random sample of five rows was a good estimate of the population statistics, even though the sample was much smaller than the full dataset.

### Task 7: Describe the results

Write a few sentences about what you found in the data. What does this tell you about the M&Ms dataset and about the act of random sampling?

in this activity, i took a random sample of five rows from the mandm's dataset and calculated the mean and standard deviation for the red M&M counts. My sample mean was 73.8, while the population mean was 72.98. The sanple standard deviation was 14.92, compared to 16.46 for the population. the results were pretty similar, even though I only used five rows for my sample. This shows that random sampling can give us a good estimate of the population, but the results will not always be exactly the same. using a larger sample could help make the results more representative of the full dataset.
